assertion.name: Serum Free Thyroxine (Free T4)

loinc_term.label: Thyroxine (T4) free [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma

assertion.notes: Free T4 is low or in the lower half of the reference interval - not necessarily frankly low, which is why it is unreliable on its own. In the untreated adult series, free T4 was within the reference range in all four patients. The 0.8-1.8 ng/dL band below is a conventional clinical laboratory reference interval with no single citable primary source (assay- and age-dependent), recorded here per the convention used in Generalized_Resistance_to_Thyroid_Hormone and Allan-Herndon-Dudley_Syndrome rather than attributed to a fabricated citation. No RTH-alpha cohort mean or median free T4 is asserted: the only large set of values located (PMID:38148509) is the median for children selected by the screening filter, and no THRA variant was found in any of them, so those numbers describe the filter's catchment rather than the disease. The marker carries the mass-concentration code used by its reference range rather than the molar code (LOINC:14920-3), so the two bindings agree.

assertion.name: Blood Eosinophil Count (BEC)
assertion.context: The most accessible biomarker in clinical practice for identifying eosinophilic asthma and predicting response to type 2 targeted biologic therapy. BEC interpretation requires contextualization, as corticosteroid exposure, biological variability, age at onset, and comorbidities influence readings.
assertion.notes: This is the disease-wide, LOINC-bound counterpart of the subtype-scoped "Eosinophils" record above, which reports eosinophilia qualitatively for the allergic asthma subtype only. The two are not duplicates: that record says eosinophils are elevated in allergic asthma, this one carries the assay binding and the count strata that biologic selection turns on. Neither supersedes the other.

readouts.interpretation: The circulating count is an indirect measure of the eosinophil arm of the type 2 response: IL-5 released at this node governs eosinophil maturation and survival, so the blood compartment tracks the node's activity. It does not measure airway eosinophilia directly.

reference_ranges.population: patients aged 12 years or older with severe asthma

The bands below are the baseline blood eosinophil strata of the DREAM/MENSA secondary analysis (PMID:27177493), reproduced as published: they partition predicted biologic response, not assay normality. Counts below roughly 500 cells/uL sit inside the conventional adult laboratory range for this analyte, which is why the lower three bands carry abnormal_flag NORMAL; that conventional upper limit is hematology practice rather than a figure any cited abstract states, so it is recorded here rather than as a bound. Eligibility thresholds differ between agents and guidelines, so do not read these bands as eligibility rules.

interpretation_bands.interpretation: At or above the count where DREAM/MENSA reported clinically relevant reductions in exacerbation frequency with mepolizumab (PMID:27177493), while still inside the conventional laboratory range for this analyte.

assertion.name: Astrocyte Plasma Proteomic Age Gap

biomarker_term.preferred_term: astrocyte plasma proteomic aging clock (age gap)

assertion.context: Blood-based cell-type-specific aging clock. Plasma proteins are mapped to their putative cell of origin using Human Protein Atlas single-cell transcriptomic data, and a machine-learning model estimates astrocyte biological age; the age gap is the difference between that estimate and chronological age. "Extreme" agers are those in the upper tail of the age-gap distribution and "youthful" agers the lower tail.
assertion.notes: Astrocyte age gap was the strongest cellular-aging predictor of incident Alzheimer disease in UK Biobank over 15 years of follow-up, and stratified risk within every APOE genotype stratum, including APOE4 homozygotes. Note that the headline 12.59-fold figure is an extreme-versus-youthful contrast; in the separate comparison against established risk factors the excess risk of extreme astrocyte aging was HR 5.16 (95% CI 4.06-6.56), comparable to APOE4 carrier status (HR 5.30) and exceeding the AD polygenic risk score (HR 2.14). This is a prognostic association from observational cohorts, not a demonstration that astrocyte aging causes Alzheimer disease.

readouts.interpretation: An elevated astrocyte age gap reports an aged astrocyte proteomic state and predicts incident Alzheimer disease years before diagnosis. It is linked to the astrocytic arm of the neuroinflammation node, but the study measures plasma protein signatures rather than brain astrocyte reactivity directly.

In the NSHD Insight-46 substudy the astrocyte age gap tracked plasma pTau-217 burden, an orthogonal blood measure of amyloid and tau pathology, linking the clock to tau pathology rather than to cognition alone.

selected_evidence.snippet: Individuals who were homozygous for APOE4 and had extreme astrocyte aging showed the highest cumulative incidence of 38.3% over 15 years of follow-up, compared to 12.6% for homozygotes with normal astrocyte aging.

term.label: factor XIII, A subunit, deficiency of

assertion.name: Plasma factor XIII-A subunit antigen
assertion.notes: Immunoreactive FXIII-A concentration, reduced in parallel with activity in the quantitative A-subunit defects that make up most of this disease. This is the measurement that assigns a patient to A-subunit rather than B-subunit deficiency. assertion.notes: The diagnostic test. Measured by a quantitative functional assay - most commonly ammonia release, in which thrombin and calcium activate FXIII and the liberated ammonia is quantified through a glutamate dehydrogenase-coupled NADH oxidation - and reported as a percentage of normal. The interpretation bands below are the activity thresholds used clinically to set prophylaxis troughs and perioperative targets; they are not a laboratory normal interval and they are drawn from narrative review rather than prospective validation, which the review itself says is the outstanding evidence gap. The biomarker is bound to the NCIT term for the measurement because NCIT's clinical-measurement branch is where this concept sits; the analyte-level LOINC codes are on the reference ranges.

assertion.notes: A secondary, not a primary, abnormality in this disease, and worth curating because it is a trap: FXIII-B antigen is also low in A-subunit deficiency, so a low FXIII-B does not mean F13B disease. assertion.name: 3-Hydroxybutyrylcarnitine (C4OH)
assertion.context: C4OH is a proposed co-primary newborn-screening marker for BKD. Because T2 also catalyses the thiolytic cleavage of acetoacetyl-CoA in extrahepatic ketolysis, D-3-hydroxybutyrate accumulates and is conjugated to C4OH. It was raised in 94% of a Chinese cohort with available values, and critically it can be elevated in patients whose C5-OH and C5:1 are normal — the false-negative pattern that causes BKD to be missed on the conventional two-marker panel. Like the other markers it is state-dependent and may normalise between crises.
assertion.notes: Described as a newborn-screening marker and as a value that normalises between crises, without a single specimen, so loinc_term binds the specimen-agnostic LOINC Part; the reference interval below is a dried-blood-spot interval and carries the DBS code.

reference_ranges.population: newborn screening reference interval used in the Chinese BKD cohort
reference_ranges.notes: Affected patients in this cohort had a median C4OH of 1.38 umol/L (range 0.26-3.58), i.e. roughly 4-fold above the upper reference limit, but the value is state-dependent and can fall back into range between crises. LOINC codes the analyte as the Part LOINC:LP19307-5 and in dried blood spot as LOINC:50102-3 (Monarch KG search for "3-Hydroxybutyrylcarnitine"); the interval is a screening reference interval, and the cohort paper says only that the C4OH cutoff is set at the 99.5 centile, so no band is drawn from it.

readouts.interpretation: Elevated C4OH reports carnitine conjugation of D-3-hydroxybutyrate accumulating behind the blocked extrahepatic ketolysis step.

selected_evidence.snippet: Notably, patients No. 4 and 11 had increased C4OH levels only, while C5OH and C5:1 levels were normal, even during the course of metabolic decompensations.

term.label: autosomal recessive severe congenital neutropenia due to G6PC3 deficiency

assertion.name: Absolute neutrophil count
assertion.context: The absolute neutrophil count (ANC) is the defining laboratory measurement of the disease. In G6PC3 deficiency the ANC is typically in the severe band (<500/uL) at diagnosis and may fluctuate only marginally, in contrast to the regular oscillation of cyclic neutropenia. It is also the response variable for both G-CSF and empagliflozin therapy.

readouts.target: Endoplasmic reticulum stress and increased myeloid apoptosis
readouts.interpretation: A falling ANC reports the net loss of maturing granulocytic precursors to apoptosis; ANC recovery is the standard endpoint for treatments aimed at the upstream metabolic lesion.

loinc_term.label: Neutrophils [#/volume] in Blood by Automated count

reference_ranges.population: adults
reference_ranges.notes: One-sided interval: chronic neutropenia is diagnosed below 1,500/uL, so only a lower bound is given. Paediatric lower limits are age-dependent and lower in infancy and in individuals of African ancestry (benign ethnic neutropenia); this interval is the adult chronic-neutropenia threshold.

interpretation_bands.name: Normal
interpretation_bands.interpretation: ANC at or above 1,500/uL is not neutropenic.

interpretation_bands.name: Mild neutropenia
interpretation_bands.interpretation: Mild neutropenia; infection risk is close to background. Some G6PC3 patients sit in this band and can be managed with prophylactic antibiotics alone.

interpretation_bands.name: Moderate neutropenia
interpretation_bands.interpretation: Moderate neutropenia with intermediate infection risk.

interpretation_bands.name: Severe neutropenia
interpretation_bands.interpretation: Severe neutropenia; the band occupied by almost all G6PC3-deficient patients at diagnosis and the threshold at which severe pyogenic infection risk rises sharply and G-CSF is indicated.

selected_evidence.snippet: Neutropenia was profound (<0.5 × 109/l) in almost all cases at diagnosis and could marginally fluctuate.

term.label: autosomal recessive severe congenital neutropenia due to G6PC3 deficiency

assertion.name: Plasma 1,5-anhydroglucitol
assertion.context: 1,5-Anhydroglucitol is an abundant, largely dietary blood polyol and the precursor from which the toxic 1,5-AG6P is generated intracellularly. Plasma 1,5-AG is not itself abnormal in G6PC3 deficiency — it is the pharmacological handle: SGLT2 inhibition blocks its renal reabsorption, lowers the plasma pool, and thereby lowers neutrophil 1,5-AG6P. Interindividual variation in 1,5-AG clearance (e.g. an SGLT5 variant) modifies disease severity.

readouts.interpretation: Plasma 1,5-AG is the upstream substrate pool; lowering it with an SGLT2 inhibitor is the direct pharmacodynamic readout of the therapy and tracks the fall in neutrophil 1,5-AG6P.

selected_evidence.snippet: which had low blood 1,5-AG levels and only required GCSF during severe infections
